chunks: What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Saʿd, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿĪsā, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام arrived in Makkah and asked me about ʿAbdullāh ibn Aʿyan. I said, “He has died.” He said, “He has died? Do you know the location of his grave?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Then come with us to his grave so that we may pray over him.” I said, “Yes.” He said, “No, rather we shall pray over him here.” Then he raised his hands in supplication, strove earnestly in the supplication, and asked Allah to have mercy on him.

key_terms.تَرَحَّمَ عَلَيْهِ: he asked Allah to have mercy on him
key_terms.نُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: we pray over him, meaning to perform prayer for the deceased
key_terms.هَاهُنَا: here, in this place rather than at the grave itself

ai.seo_question: Can one pray for and invoke mercy upon a deceased person without being present at the grave?
ai.summary: This report describes Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام responding to the death of ʿAbdullāh ibn Aʿyan with concern, du'a, and mercy. It indicates the practice of praying for the deceased even from a place away from the grave, and highlights earnest supplication for a departed believer.
